title: App Store Connect API key and signing secrets in GitHub Actions
summary: The Owner holds an App Store Connect API key (confirmed 2026-09-15). Add it to CI secrets so ios-build can sign with Xcode cloud-managed signing and upload internal TestFlight builds from M1: without a Mac, TestFlight is the only path to the Owner's devices. Values live only in GitHub secrets; never on the Bot VM.

acceptance_tests.test: Repository secrets `ASC_KEY_ID`, `ASC_ISSUER_ID`, and `ASC_KEY_P8_BASE64` (the .p8 file, base64-encoded in one line) exist; the key has the App Manager role (Admin also works); repository variable `APPLE_TEAM_ID` holds the Apple Team ID.
acceptance_tests.evidence: secrets and variables page screenshot with values hidden

acceptance_tests.test: An App Store Connect app record exists for com.sparkforgelabs.giganticjourneys named Gigantic Journeys (this also reserves the name), with an internal TestFlight group set to automatic distribution containing the Owner's Apple ID.
The key never appears in the repo, tickets, issues, chat, logs, or the Bot VM; the workflow deletes its copy after each run.
acceptance_tests.evidence: secret-scan green; workflow step 'Remove the key material'

acceptance_tests.test: After M0-UNITY-01 merges, set repository variable `TESTFLIGHT_ENABLED=true`; the first build installs on the Owner's iPhone from TestFlight.
